newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says Germany will respect Maastricht.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says Germany will respect Maastricht.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday he was confident Germany would respect conditions in the Maastricht Treaty on monetary union.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, de Silguy said European Union nations could not be allowed to resort to "tricks" to meet criteria in the treaty.

"I am confident Germany will be ready in due time as will a lot of member states," he said. "It will not be possible to find tricks to respect the criteria and the rules will be the same for all member states."
De Silguy declined to comment on a decision by the German government to revalue the country's gold reserves to help it bolster public finances, saying he had not seen the details of the measures.
But he said that in principle he was pleased by the German government's determination to do what was needed to be ready on time for EMU.
"I welcome the will of the German government to take the necessary measures to fulfil their commitments," he said.
He said the new European single currency would be strong and stable since members will respect the criteria.
"The euro will be a strong and stable currency. That is the reason we will strictly apply all the conditions in the treaty," he said.
"There are five criteria and five reference values, but only reference values," de Silguy, who was speaking in English, said.

"There are some other conditions and we have the necessity to prove for each member state that the convergence will be durable, sustainable and when we apply the treaty, we take into consideration all the conditions."
